title: Hot Cocoa Mix

drivers.name: TikTok trend
drivers.evidence: Product trending on TikTok with no historical precedent; recent weekly sales up 22% vs prior 4 weeks. Noise-adjusted effect of similar viral events not measurable. Shrunk to 15% due to thin evidence.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 30.3. No events or promotions in target week. Price increased 3.4% to $5.20, which typically suppresses demand; past promotions show noise-adjusted lift of x1.0, suggesting price changes have little effect. However, TikTok trend is a new, untested driver. No historical data on social media spikes. The recent sales trend is rising (trend_13_vs_prior_13_pct=16.2), but baseline already reflects this. Classical model suggests no lift, consistent with noise-adjusted history. Apply cautious uplift for untested viral effect, shrink toward 1.0 due to lack of evidence. No downside drivers.

brief:
PRODUCT: Hot Cocoa Mix | category Grocery | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.20 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.03)
  planner notes: Product is trending on TikTok

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 30.3 | 5%-95%: 4.6 - 46.8 | 10%-90%: 9.0 - 46.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
